text:
### Observed differences

- The branch chosen after A15 flipped. Earlier, about 75 in 100 of A15's outgoing transitions went to A16, A17 or A18 (roughly 27, 23 and 26 per 100) and about 25 in 100 to A19, A20 or A21; in the later window the shares reversed, with about 76 in 100 going to A19, A20 or A21 (about 25, 22 and 29 per 100) and about 24 in 100 to A16, A17 or A18. [DIR001]
- Participation swapped accordingly: A16, A17 and A18 each appeared in about 75 in 100 traces earlier but only about 25 in 100 later, while A19, A20 and A21 each rose from about 25 to about 76 in 100 traces. A15 and A25 appeared in essentially every trace in both windows. [REL001, REL009, REL012, REL014, REL018, REL021]
- The two groups are strict alternatives: pairs such as A16 with A19, or A17 with A20, never occur in the same trace in either window. [REL009, REL014, REL018]
- Group-internal behaviour is preserved: A16, A17 and A18 co-occurred in about 75 in 100 traces earlier, appearing in both orders in similar shares (no fixed order), and rarely share a trace later (about 25 in 100); A19, A20 and A21 show the mirror image, co-occurring in about 76 in 100 later versus 25 earlier, again with no fixed order. A15 precedes whichever group is active (A before B in about 75–76 in 100 traces). [REL001, REL004, REL007, REL013, REL022, REL025]
- A25 changed partners: earlier it co-occurred with A16, A17 or A18 in about 75 in 100 traces (A16 before A25 in about 43, interleaved in about 32); later it co-occurs with A19, A20 or A21 in about 76 in 100 (A19 before A25 in about 40, interleaved in about 36), while the old trio rarely does. [REL012, REL017, REL021, REL024, REL026, REL027]
- The A15-to-A20 step distance shortened: earlier the pair was most often 3 positions apart (52 in 100); later, gaps of 1–2 positions dominate (about 66 in 100 combined) and 3-position gaps fell to about 34 in 100. [LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

In the later window the process usually takes the other branch after A15: the unordered group A19, A20, A21 — executed together in about 76 in 100 traces, up from about 25 — now follows A15 in place of the unordered group A16, A17, A18, which fell to about 25 in 100 traces from about 75, and A25 now co-occurs with the new group instead of the old one. Since all six activities and both groups are observed in substantial shares in both windows and only the shares between the alternatives moved, this reads as existing paths being taken with different frequencies rather than activities being added, removed or repositioned. Supporting signs: the redistribution of A15's outgoing transitions matches the participation flip; each group keeps its internal no-fixed-order structure and A15 still precedes the active group; and the A15-to-A20 distance shortened as expected if A20 now follows A15 directly more often. The 29 qualifying items (all control-flow) far exceed the roughly 0.41 expected without change, and every difference is larger than in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits. The evidence cannot distinguish a changed routing decision at A15 from a shifted mix of two pre-existing case variants that each use one group, and the relation items describe the same traces, so they are not independent confirmations. [DIR001, REL001, REL004, REL007, REL009, REL012, REL022, REL024, LAG001]
